question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, __(A) he listened to his father's stories__ about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, __(B) an attachment that is shown__ in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, __(C) where he worked__ as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, __(D) where he became interested in the media of sculpture__. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) __(B) must qualify__ as well. They both __(C) can change__ our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both __(E) are__ useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

question.passageWithMarkers: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait __(A) that kept us alive__ when we were living on the savannas but __(B) that can prevent happiness__ in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on __(C) what's going wrong__ (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, __(E) train yourself__ to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

question.passageWithMarkers: When we see something, we naturally and automatically __(A) break it up__ into shapes, colors, and concepts that we __(B) have learned__ through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail __(C) struggle__ to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely __(D) undermine__ the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing __(E) is__ not believing.

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 『making time for exercise』는 동명사구로 주어 자리에 올바르게 쓰였고, 단수 취급되어 'is'와 수일치가 이루어졌으므로 어법상 문제가 없습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 『there's no room』은 'there is no room'의 축약형으로 주어-동사 수일치가 올바르며, 비격식체 문장에서 자연스럽게 사용됩니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 『do』는 관계대대명사 지시 관계에서 주격 관계대명사 'that'이 선행사 'tasks'를 받아 생략된 형태로, 'tasks are'라는 완전한 절의 동사 역할을 합니다. 동사 'are'가 이미 존재하므로 'do'는 불필요한 삽입으로 오해할 수 있으나, 여기서 'do'는 강조 용법이 아니라 'tasks that do are'라는 구조 자체가 성립하지 않습니다. 그러나 실제 원문에는 'do'가 없으므로 (D) 자체는 원문대로 'are'만 존재합니다. 문제 출제 시 (D)는 원문 그대로 제시되었으므로 오류가 아닙니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 『can improve』는 조동사 'can' 뒤에 동사 원형 'improve'가 온 올바른 형태이며, 주어 'Incorporating quick exercises'와의 수일치에도 문제가 없습니다.

question.explanation: (B)는 문장 첫머리에서 소문자 'between'으로 시작하고 있습니다. 영어 문장에서 마침표 뒤 새 문장의 첫 단어는 반드시 대문자로 시작해야 합니다. 원문에서는 마침표 뒤 'Between'으로 대문자 표기되어야 하나, 에 따라 'between'으로 소문자 처리하여 어법상 비문으로 구성하였습니다. 나머지 (A), (C), (D), (E)는 모두 문법적으로 정확한 표현입니다.
keyPoints: 문장 첫 단어는 대문자로 시작하는 것이 절대적인 영어 철자법 규칙이다.
소문자로 시작한 (B)는 표준 문법을 위반하며, 유일한 어법상 오류이다.
수험생은 주로 동사 형태나 구문에 집중하지만, 이 문제는 기초적인 철자 및 대소문자 규칙을 킬러 문항으로 활용하였다.
나머지 네 곳은 모두 문법적으로 완벽하여 함정에 빠지기 쉽다.
question.passageWithMarkers: For many of us, __(A) making time for exercise is a continuing challenge__. __(B) between__, it often feels like __(C) there's no room__ in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores __(E) can improve__ your health.

passageText: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise hadn't changed you paid it no attention.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They tended to call the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 'the experience of ~ing'에서 of는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사 noticing이 와야 한다. 'noticing'은 동명사로 올바르게 사용되었다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 'Your auditory areas'는 복수 주어이므로 were predicting이 쓰였으며, 과거 시점에서 진행 중이던 동작을 나타내기에 과거진행 시제가 적절하다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 'tend to + 동사원형'은 '~하는 경향이 있다'는 관용 표현으로, to call은 올바른 형태이다. 주어 They(사람)가 경찰에 전화하는 행위를 나타낸다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 'the trains used to run'에서 used to는 '과거에 ~하곤 했다'는 조동사로, 뒤에 동사원형 run이 와야 한다. 전체적으로 문법에 맞다.

question.explanation: 정답은 (C)이다. (C) 'hadn't changed'가 속한 문장은 'as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention'이어야 한다. 'as long as'는 조건의 부사절을 이끌며, 과거 사실을 조건으로 할 때는 과거 시제(didn't change)가 쓰여야 한다. 과거완료(hadn't changed)는 이 문맥에서 불필요하며 시제 일치를 깨뜨려 비문이 된다. 따라서 'hadn't changed'를 'didn't change'로 고쳐야 한다. (A)는 동명사, (B)는 과거진행 시제와 수일치, (D)는 'tend to + 동사원형' 구문, (E)는 'used to + 동사원형' 구문으로 모두 올바르다.
keyPoints: (C) 조건 부사절에서 과거 시제와 과거완료의 구분 — as long as 뒤에 과거 사실 조건은 과거 시제 사용
(A) 전치사 of 뒤에 오는 동명사와 to부정사의 구분 — of는 동명사만 허용
(E) 조동사 used to와 동사원형의 결합 — used to 다음에는 항상 동사원형
question.passageWithMarkers: We have all had the experience of suddenly __(A) noticing__ that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas __(B) were predicting__ its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended __(D) to call__ around the time the trains __(E) used__ to run past their apartments.

passageText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 'any more time than it would'는 비교급 'more'와 부정문 'any'가 결합한 정상 표현으로, '그것이 (할) 시간보다 더 많은 시간'이라는 의미를 전달하므로 어법상 문제가 없습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 'contrary to popular belief'는 전치사구로서 '대중의 믿음과는 반대로'라는 의미로 부사구 역할을 하며, 문장 내에서 정상적으로 사용되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 'your phone pressed to your ear'는 'with + 목적어 + 과거분사(pressed)' 구문으로, '전화기를 귀에 댄 채로'라는 의미의 부대상황을 나타내는 정상적인 표현입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 'While doing the laundry'는 'While you are doing the laundry'에서 주어와 be동사가 생략된 분사구문으로, 주절의 주어(you)와 능동 관계를 이루므로 어법상 올바릅니다.

question.explanation: (D) 밑줄 'than it would when done'은 비교구문에서 오류입니다. 이 문장의 골격은 'It doesn't take up any more time than it would (take up time) when (you are) done with your phone pressed to your ear'로, 'it'은 'doing the laundry'를 가리키며 비교 대상은 '세탁 시간'입니다. 그러나 'done'은 수동 분사로서 'it'이 '완료되다'는 의미를 강제하는데, 이는 '세탁이 시간을 차지하다(take up time)'라는 능동 동작과 충돌합니다. 따라서 'than it would when done'은 비문이며, 올바르게 고치려면 'than it does when you are doing it' 또는 능동 분사구문 'than it would when doing it'을 써야 합니다.
keyPoints: (D) 비교구문에서 수동 분사 'done'의 오용 — 능동 의미의 동작을 수동태로 표현한 비문
(E) 'with + 목적어 + 과거분사' 구문 — 부대상황 표현의 정상적인 구조 이해
(B) 분사구문의 주어 일치 — 주절 주어와의 능동 관계 확인
question.passageWithMarkers: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, __(A) contrary to popular belief__. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. __(B) While doing the laundry__, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up __(C) any more time than it would__ would when done__ with __(E) your phone pressed to your ear__. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중에서 **어법상 틀린 것**을 고르시오.

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the distance.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: not too much time goes by between oil changes

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: it's been a while since you've spoken

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 「현재완료 + in ages」는 ‘오랜만에’라는 의미의 자연스러운 표현입니다. 주어 we와 haven’t spoken의 수일치도 적절하며, to 전치사가 사람 목적어를 받는 구조(전치사 목적어 생략)도 문법에 맞습니다. 따라서 올바른 표현입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 「be kept up」은 ‘유지되다’라는 의미의 수동태로서, 관계(relationships)를 주어로 받아 ‘관계는 유지된다’고 해석됩니다. 시제와 수일치 모두 문제없습니다. 따라서 올바른 표현입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 「how much time goes by」에서 동사 goes는 주어 time(단수)에 일치하고 있으며, 부사절 내 현재시제도 적절합니다. ‘(시간이) 흐르다’라는 의미의 구동사로서 사용된 것도 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 올바른 표현입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 「bother + -ing」는 ‘~하느라 애쓰다/수고하다’의 의미로 쓰이는 정형 표현입니다. 조동사 shouldn’t와 결합하여 ‘~할 수고를 할 필요가 없다’는 뜻을 명확히 전달합니다. 따라서 올바른 표현입니다.

question.explanation: (E) "you haven't spoken"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "you've spoken"로 고쳐야 한다. 「since + 주어 + 현재완료」 구문은 ‘~한 이후로/~한 지 … 되었다’라는 시간을 나타냅니다. 이때 ‘~한 지’는 since 이하의 동작이 **과거에 끝난 상태**임을 전제하므로, since 다음에는 **과거 시제** 또는 **현재완료가 아닌 과거의 상황**을 나타내는 표현이 와야 합니다. 원문에서는 ‘it’s been a while since you’ve spoken’이라 쓰여 ‘당신이 말을 한 이후로’라는 의미를 현재완료로 표현했는데, 이는 **‘말을 한 상태(완료)’**가 아니라 **‘마지막으로 말을 한 시점(과거)’**을 가리켜야 하므로 **과거 시제(since you spoke)** 또는 **since you last spoke**가 올바릅니다. 따라서 (E)는 어법상 비문입니다.
keyPoints: since + 시점(과거)
현재완료가 아닌 과거 시제 사용
since + 과거 시제 / since + last + 과거
‘~한 이후(로)’는 과거의 한 시점을 나타냄
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we __(A) haven't spoken to in ages__, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time __(C) goes by__ between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you __(D) shouldn't bother calling__ someone just because it's been a while since __(E) you haven't spoken__; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.

passageText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.
